chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Basir said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah on a Friday, and I had already prayed Friday prayer and Asr prayer. I found him had 'baha' (gathered/combined), meaning he had combined [prayers]. So he came out to me wearing a milhafah (a large cloak). Then he called his maid and ordered her to place water for him and pour it over him. I said to him, 'May Allah perfect you, have you performed ghusl?' He said, 'I have not performed ghusl yet, nor have I prayed.' I said to him, 'We have prayed Dhuhr and Asr together.' He said, 'There is no harm [in that].'
Because delaying Dhuhr beyond the time of the sun's zenith is not prohibited if there is an excuse, and we have only made it obligatory [to pray at the specific time] for one who has no excuse.

key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٍ: A large cloak or wrap worn by the Imams

ai.seo_question: Can Friday prayer be combined with Asr prayer if there is a valid excuse like needing ghusl?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that delaying Dhuhr beyond its primary time (zawal) is permissible when a valid excuse exists, such as the time required for ghusl. He distinguishes this from the obligatory combination (jam') for those without an excuse, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding prayer times based on practical circumstances. This hadith is foundational for understanding the distinction between *jam' taqdim* (early combination) and *jam' ta'khir* (delayed combination) in Shia fiqh.
